proposed_changes.rationale: Claiming prospective validation when validation was actually retrospective on previously collected data is a misrepresentation of study design that directly affects scientific validity (MLGG dimension 1 cohort/design integrity). Misleading claim about validation type can constitute undisclosed test-tuning concern if model development overlapped with the data collection period (Mamba introduced 2023, data 2021-2023).
Incorrect novelty claim is a polish/terminology issue, not methodological. Easily corrected by rewording; does not affect the validity of reported results.

Using a random split over 20 years of EHR data when temporal drift in medical practice is well-documented constitutes a form of temporal leakage / unrealistic deployment estimate — directly violates MLGG split protocol assumptions. The concern is not merely 'should do temporal split too' but that the original estimate is fundamentally not deployment-relevant.

Death rate 1.3% with no PR curve / AUPRC for the rare-outcome endpoint falls squarely into the rubric's HIGH category (class-imbalance not handled on rare outcomes). AUROC alone is well-known to be optimistic at this prevalence.

Patient flow, consecutiveness, and missing-data handling are reporting completeness issues (MLGG dim 8). They affect interpretation but the underlying methodology is not broken; cleanly addressed by adding flow diagrams. Fits MEDIUM (should-fix-but-not-invalidate).
Adherence/retention reporting is a completeness issue, not a methodological flaw in the model. Missing wear-time stats are MEDIUM polish/clarification rather than HIGH methodological risk.

The reviewer is challenging the motivation/premise (whether leakage exists in classification models), not pointing to an actual data-leakage flaw in the work. This is a framing/justification critique, not a scientific-validity threat. No CRITICAL trigger from rubric (no MLGG-F02/S01/fabrication/test tuning).

Reproducibility (code/data availability) is critically important but does not by itself invalidate the scientific claims. Rubric reserves CRITICAL for scientific-validity threats (leakage, F02, S01, fabrication, undisclosed tuning). Missing code/data fits HIGH — methodologically important and fixable by release.

Overparameterization with 117 candidate features and 87 cases is a serious overfitting / selection-on-test risk but the rubric reserves CRITICAL for data leakage, MLGG-F02 future info, MLGG-S01 cross-split, fabricated cohort, or undisclosed test-tuning. This is best classified as HIGH (methodologically important but fixable by regularization/nested CV).

If Figure 4d/7d are genuinely training-set performance presented as prognostic evidence, that constitutes evaluation on data used in fitting — equivalent to test-set contamination in a prognostic claim. The reviewer flagged a fundamental validity concern; until clarified as CV, it is CRITICAL. Author response says they relabeled as CV — but the original-paper concern severity should reflect the pre-fix risk.

Adding LDpred2 baseline + runtime comparison is a model-comparison completeness ask. Author already shows reasonable comparators; this is enhancement rather than a methodological deficiency. Fits MEDIUM (missing ablation).

Lacking factor-correlation analysis to explain prediction-quality variance across 457 traits is missing supporting analysis rather than a flaw in the primary results. Better fits MEDIUM (missing ablation/subgroup analysis).

Clinical-utility / harm concern about over-treatment is critically important clinically but does not match rubric CRITICAL triggers (leakage, F02, S01, fabrication, undisclosed tuning). It is a clinical_metrics_gate concern about clinical actionability — fits HIGH (methodologically important, fixable by stratifying by clinical significance and revising workflow as authors did).
